proof_summary: The word used in the statement is the tenth substitution iterate padded by 1’s; its length is at most \(4^{10}\), so it has at most \(4^{10}\) zeros and the definition yields \(a(4^{10}+1)=1\). Since \(r=(3+\sqrt3)/3\ge1\), this gives \((4^{10}+1)r-a(4^{10}+1)\ge4^{10}>2\), contradicting the proposed upper bound.
